text:
maria: quick follow-up on the microburst fastpath RFC. i'm trying to capture operational gotchas before i finalize the doc. main goals: keep small requests low-latency without creating a ton of tiny queue islands.

tj: high level +1. two immediate risks: (1) cache pointer hoarding -> starvation, (2) CPU/kernel churn from too many tiny launches.

maria: agreed. thinking of a hybrid: a soft-lease window for fastpath requests + admission tokens that limit concurrent small-windows per GPU. soft-lease allows preempt/requeue.

anya: what does preempt mean exactly? restart from scratch or continue later with preserved prefix state?
maria: ideally preserve prefix/KV pointers if possible. but if we evict, we requeue as cold with a backoff. preempt path should include a small backoff jitter to avoid thundering.

tj: how do we decide which requests are preemptable? we can't preempt something that has high cache-reuse value. maybe a cheap heuristic: protect requests with kv_touch_count >= N or protected_bit=true set at admission.

anya: that matches my mental model. we can compute kv_touch_count in admission probe and flip protected_bit if above threshold. protected requests bypass soft-lease preemption.

maria: config sketch for tenant opt-in:

small_fastpath_enabled=true
fastpath_concurrency=6  # tokens per GPU
soft_lease_ms=40        # adaptive baseline
kv_protect_threshold=3
preempt_requeue_priority="age-boosted"

tj: soft_lease_ms=40 seems fine as a baseline but make it adaptive: max(40, p95_warmup_ms). runtime should feed p95_warmup into scheduler.

anya: telemetry we need: kernel_launch_rate, fastpath_success_rate (no-preempt), kv_touch_histogram, reprovision_requeue_count, tail_latency_99.

maria: and a cost model: extra_kernel_launchs_per_minute * cost_per_launch approximation. we should expose in console as "fastpath_unit_cost" so product can evaluate tradeoffs.

tj: rollout playbook: enable in canary with concurrency=1, observe for 30m. guard rails: if kernel_launch_rate > baseline*2 and throughput drops by >10% -> rollback. Also watch kv_eviction_rate spike.

ops-bot: note: i can create the feature flag and a dashboard with the listed metrics. canary cluster request?

maria: yes please, ops-bot create flag fastpath_microburst.canary and dashboard with kernel_launch_rate, fastpath_latency_p95/p99, kv_eviction_rate, throughput_rps. add alert if kernel_launch_rate > 2x baseline for 5m.

anya: one more tradeoff: small-window fastpath can reduce end-to-end latency but it may hurt prefix caching reuse across requests. measuring "prefix_reuse_ratio" before/after will be important. if we see reuse ratio drop > 15% then we might tighten kv_protect_threshold.

tj: also consider a backpressure signal from runtime: if kernel_launch_rate high, runtime can return ADMIT_THROTTLE hint. scheduler should honor that by reducing fastpath tokens per GPU. simple control loop.

maria: good. put that in RFC: two-way hints: scheduler->runtime admission_hint(concurrency_hint), runtime->scheduler pressure_hint(kernel_launch_rate, kv_eviction_rate).

anya: testing note: include synthetic workloads with short prompt bursts and longer prompts mixed. ensure preempt/requeue preserves correctness for streaming clients.

maria: i'll draft RFC with these sections: motivation, API sketches (admission_hint, pressure_hint, kv_protect_bit), telemetry + cost model, rollout playbook, rollback thresholds, and sample tenant config. will ping for reviews.

tj: i'll review the control loop and metrics.

anya: i'll look at kv protection heuristics and streaming edge cases.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-7893 for dashboard and INF-7894 for feature flag. :robot_face:

maria: thanks all. i'll post the RFC link when ready and include canary test steps.
